top_signals.title: Saudi Arabia Halts Energy Sites as Houthis Claim New Attacks
top_signals.summary:
Saudi Arabia halted several energy facilities in the south, as the Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed fresh strikes on the kingdom. The Yemen-based Houthis said they targeted Saudi Aramco’s facilities in Abha, Najran and Jazan with ballistic missiles and drones, the group’s military spokesperson said in a statement. The attacks caused fires at several locations, and efforts were ongoing to contain the blazes, the Saudi energy ministry said on X, without naming the facilities.

While the targets appear to include infrastructure that supply the local Saudi demand, repeated attacks on Jazan, where a major refinery is located, are a concern for the oil market. For the latest, we speak with Becca Wasser, Defense Lead for Bloomberg Economics. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Heinekin Highlights Nonalcoholic Beer, Serena Williams in US Open Partnership
top_signals.summary: Maggie Timoney, CEO of Heinekin USA, said Heinekin's 0.0 nonalcoholic beer has seen success because consumers are looking to moderate their alcohol consumption, even if they're not looking to cut it out entirely. Timoney said that the beverage company wanted to honor the history of the US Open and the six championships won by Serena Williams in their partnership with the tennis star.  (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: Luxury Whiskey Bets on Ready-Made Cocktails
top_signals.summary: Julie Macklowe, the Founder of the luxury whiskey brand Macklowe, joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about how tariffs on liquor ultimately punish American consumers through higher prices, and may even be contributing to younger generations drinking less. She also explains why convenience is driving her latest bet: a premium, ready-to-serve whiskey cocktail designed to make the traditionally "snobby" category more accessible. (Source: Bloomberg)
